smokers treated with acupuncture exhibited significantly greater reductions in craving and exhibited reduced activation in the mPFC (executive function), the premotor cortex (motor preparation), the amygdala (stimulus-reward learning), the hippocampus (prior experience), and the medial thalamus (reward) when viewing smoking-related visual cues compared with smokers treated with the sham treatment

spans.text: In summary, smokers treated with acupuncture exhibited significantly greater reductions in craving and exhibited reduced activation in the mPFC (executive function), the premotor cortex (motor preparation), the amygdala (stimulus-reward learning), the hippocampus (prior experience), and the medial thalamus (reward) when viewing smoking-related visual cues compared with smokers treated with the sham treatment.
